descriptionChirho: Qal stem expressing the intransitive state of growing faint, weak, or exhausted, used of physical or emotional collapse.
Hitpael reflexive stem expressing the experience of fainting, swooning, or growing faint upon oneself, often in contexts of emotional or physical overwhelm.
Hifil causative-factitive stem indicating becoming or being made feeble, used in temporal clauses describing the onset of weakness.
Nifal passive stem expressing being overcome or seized by faintness, with the subject as the one acted upon by exhaustion.
Substantivized nominal or participial form used with the article to denote persons or things that are feeble, weak, or faint.
